newsitem.title: INDIA: Reserve Bank sees India real GDP growth at 6.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Reserve Bank sees India real GDP growth at 6.8 pct.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RB) said it expected India to record a 6.8 perecnt growth in GDP for the year ending March 31, 1997, but said a slowdown in industrial growth was a cause for concern.

Industrial production -- manufacturing sector and capital goods in particular -- in 1995/96 (April-March) was impressive, the RBI said in its "Report on Currency and Finance, 1995-96," released on Monday.
"These factors point to the feasibility of real GDP growth during 1996/97 to be around 6.8 percent as forecast by the CSO (Central Statistics Organisation)," it said.
It said the current account deficit is expected to be lower than the two percent of GDP originally envisaged.
RBI said the major highlight of economic development during 1995/96 (April-March) was the continued high real GDP growth and the moderation in inflation rate.
"The quick estimates released by the CSO in January 1997 place the real GDP growth rate for 1994/95 at 7.2 percent and for 1995/96 at 7.1 percent," the RBI said.
It said the impressive growth in 1995/96 stemmed mainly from high growth in industrial and service sectors. In 1994/95, growth was widespread across all sectors, it said.
The foreign currency assets of the RBI remain comfortable at around $19.8 billion, the RBI report said.
But the RBI said economic developments during the year also raised several concerns.
"These relate to slowdown in industrial growth, high interest rates, both nominal and real, and decline in export growth rate," RBI said.
